content.title: Markets News, March 31, 2026: Stocks End Weak Quarter on High Note as Investors Optimistic Iran War May End Soon; Dow Soars More Than 1,100 Points
content.text: 0 seconds of 0 secondsVolume 0%Loading ad00:2500:0000:33 How to Reach Financial Freedom: 12 Habits to Get You There Stocks ended sharply higher Tuesday amid renewed hopes that the Iran war could be near an end, but major indexes nevertheless posted their worst quarterly performance in nearly four years. The tech-heavy Nasdaq, benchmark S&P 500, and blue-chip Dow Jones Industrial Average finished up a respective 3.8%, 2.9%, and 2.5%, with the Dow adding 1,125 points. Still, the three major indexes registered their worst quarterly performance since the second quarter of 2022. The Nasdaq, S&P 500, and Dow closed the first quarter of 2026 down a respective 7.1%, 4.6%, and 3.6% after sinking this month following the beginning of the Middle East conflict Feb. 28. Late Monday, The Wall Street Journal reported that Trump told aides that he was willing to end the war with Iran, now in its fifth week, without full reopening the important Strait of Hormuz shipping channel. Late Tuesday, Trump told reporters that U.S. forces would likelu be leaving Iran in "two or three weeks." West Texas Intermediate crude futures, the U.S. oil benchmark, were down nearly 1% to $102 a barrel at 4 p.m. ET, while the most heavily traded contract of Brent crude futures, the global benchmark, was near $104. Meanwhile, U.S. gasoline prices hit $4 a gallon on average, AAA said. The yield on the 10-year Treasury note, which affects interest rates on all sorts of consumer loans, slipped below 4.30% from yesterday's close below 4.36%. The yield had ended last Friday near 4.44%, its highest closing level since last July. Gold futures advanced 3.4% to around $4,710 an ounce but remain well off their peak of above $5,625 an ounce set on Jan. 29. The U.S. Dollar Index, which tracks the value of the greenback against a basket of currencies, was down 0.6% to 99.90. Bitcoin rose to $67,700 from overnight lows below $66,000. Shares of all the Magnificent Seven tech giants ended comfortably higher after they finished mixed yesterday. Meta Platforms (META), which led the group's advances at around 2% Monday, closed up 6.7% further to again pace the septet. Marvell Technology (MRVL) shares soared nearly 13% to lead the Nasdaq after it announced a strategic partnership with—and $2 billion investment from—Nvidia (NVDA). Shares of the world's most valuable company advanced 5.6%. Spice maker McCormick & Co. (MKC) shares sank more than 6% after it agreed to combine with Unilever's (UL) Foods business to create what it called "a preeminent global flavor-focused company." Shares of Unilever, the parent of mayonnaise brand Hellmann's, fell 5%. Nike (NKE) stock advanced more than 3% ahead of its earnings report after the bell. Nike Stock Slides as Company Projects Sales Decline March 31, 2026 07:26 PM EDT Nike's stock is tumbling on signs of stumbling blocks in the company's turnaround. Shares of Nike (NKE) were recently down 9% in extended trading Tuesday after the athletic apparel giant told investors it expects revenue to decline 2% to 4% in the current quarter, when analysts were calling for growth. CEO Elliott Hill said during the company earnings call that its turnaround is "taking longer than I'd like," amid pressure from higher tariffs and headwinds in China that offset gains in North America. CFO Matt Friend said Nike expects sales in China to fall 20% in its fiscal fourth quarter, after registering a 10% decline in the third quarter. Hill said that going forward, Nike plans to take a more localized approach to its operations in China, after becoming "clearer on the structural challenges" in the region. Friend warned that disruptions in the Middle East, rising oil prices, and “other factors that could impact either input costs or consumer behavior” could also weigh on Nike's results this quarter. Nike's forecast overshadowed its better-than-expected earnings. Nike posted earnings per share of $0.35 on roughly flat revenue of $11.3 billion for the fiscal third quarter, both of which topped analysts' estimates compiled by Visible Alpha. Executives said Nike looks forward to offering more details on how its efforts and longer-term outlook later this year, at the company's investor day in the fall. Shares of Nike were down about 17% for 2026 through Tuesday's close. -Kara Greenberg Major Indexes End Sharply Lower for Month, Quarter Despite Strong Results Today March 31, 2026 04:08 PM EDT Even with a spectacular performance today, major stock indexes ended March sharply lower for the month—and quarter. The Nasdaq Composite, S&P 500, and Dow Jones Industrial Average finished up 3.8%, 2.9%, and 2.5% Tuesday, with the Dow adding more than 1,100 points. Still, the Nasdaq finished down 4.8% for March and 7.1% for the first quarter of 2026. The S&P 500 ended 5.1% lower this month and 4.6% in Q1, while the Dow concluded down 5.4% in March and 3.6% for the quarter. TradingView Snap Shares Soar as Activist Announces Stake, Proposes Changes March 31, 2026 03:05 PM EDT Irenic Capital Management has some suggestions on how to "save" Snap Inc. Shareholders are optimistic it can. Shares of Snap (SNAP) soared 15% in recent trading after Irenic sent a letter to Evan Spiegel, the Snapchat parent's co-founder and CEO Evan Spiegel, outlining whatt it called "actionable steps to unlock value." Snap shares were priced at $17 each during its IPO in March 2017, but closed yesterday at just $4.02. Irenic wrote that it believes the firm "could be worth at least $26.37 per share or $35 billion following value-enhancing steps," including spinning or shutting Specs, its AI eyewear unit; aligning employee incentives; and focusing on using AI to improve ad monetization. Snapchat parent Snap Inc.'s shares soared 15% Tuesday but still are down more than 40% this year. Matthias Balk / picture alliance via Getty Images Irenic, which said that it has built "an economic interest in ~2.5% of Snap's Class A shares," attached to the letter to Spiegel a presentation called "Snap Back to Reality: Save Snap Now," and told him that "we have no doubt that your second act, Saving Snap, the company, can be even more impressive than building Snap, the product." Even with today's sharp gains, Snap shares are down more than 40% year-to-date. Warren Buffett Says He's Still Making Investment Calls at Berkshire—and Just Made a Mystery Buy March 31, 2026 02:31 PM EDT So much for the Oracle of Omaha's retirement. Three months after handing over his role as CEO of Berkshire Hathaway (BRK.A, BRK.B) to Greg Abel, the 95-year-old investor told CNBC in a televised interview Tuesday that he still comes into the office every day, decides about major investments, and recently bought something new—though he declined to say what. "I can still contribute a tiny bit," Buffett said. Berkshire bought $17 billion in Treasury bills this week, adding to its sizable cash reserves, which Buffett says he could deploy if markets fall significantly. Johannes EISELE / Getty Images Clearly, stepping back from the top job hasn't meant stepping back from the market. Buffett said he calls Mark Millard, Berkshire's director of financial assets, each morning before the opening bell to talk through what's moving. The trades follow those conversations. But he's keeping Abel in the loop. "I won't make any [investments] that Greg [Abel] thinks are wrong," Buffett said. "Greg gets the sheet every day," he said, referring to Berkshire's daily record of investment activity. Read the full article here. -Peter Gratton Memory Stocks Were One of 2025's Hottest Trades. Now They've Cooled Off. What's Next? March 31, 2026 02:02 PM EDT No one stays on top forever. That goes for the hottest stocks in the AI trade, too. Memory stocks, many which were among last year's best performers in the S&P 500—and which continued to climb to start 2026—have slumped in the past two weeks. Shares of Micron (MU) are down nearly 30% since closing at an all-time high on March 18. Sandisk (SNDK) and Western Digital (WDC), the latter which was spun off from the former early last year, have dropped 22% and 19%, respectively, from their own highs a day later. Shares of memory chip giant Micron are down about 30% in the last two weeks. Kiyoshi Ota / Bloomberg via Getty Images Memory stocks have been whacked by a combination of forces. First, dynamic random access memory (DRAM) prices, which soared over the past year as booming demand from AI data centers exacerbated a supply shortage, are by some measures softening. According to a Citigroup note Tuesday, spot DRAM prices are down 6% since mid-March. Citi attributes those declines to Google’s announcement last week of TurboQuant, a method of compressing data that improves the efficiency of an AI models’ memory recall. Read the full article here. -Colin Laidley Gold Had a Disappointing First Quarter. Here's Why Wall Street Is Sticking to Its Forecasts March 31, 2026 01:40 PM EDT Thinking about fleeing gold after a tough start to the year? Some experts think you might be getting the timing wrong. Though the precious metal has rallied furiously over the past two years, doubling during that period as buying by central banks and investors turned it into a momentum trade, it's now set to post its worst monthly performance since 2008. While gold is up about 7% in the first quarter, prices have declined since the start of the war in Iran, disappointing investors who expected the haven asset to behave like one in times of travail. Gold has risen in the first quarter, but it's cooled from recent years. CFOTO/Future Publishing via Getty Images Now investors are starting to bail, as outbound fund flows in the popular SPDR Gold Trust (GLD) over the last few weeks indicate. But Wall Street experts are saying it's not the time to abandon ship. (Gold was rising Tuesday.) Read the full article here. -Crystal Kim Gas Prices Cross $4 for the First Time Since 2022—See What You'll Pay at the Pump in Your State March 31, 2026 01:26 PM EDT Oil prices remain elevated as the Iran conflict drags on, continuing to put upward pressure on fuel costs. That sustained strength in crude is pushing gasoline prices to new highs for drivers across the country. The national average for regular gasoline edged up another 3 cents Tuesday to $4.02 per gallon, the highest level since September 2022. Prices are now up more than a dollar since March 1, when the national average was $2.98. Based on AAA data, the March surge marks the fastest 30-day increase in gas prices in more than five years, underscoring how quickly costs have climbed this month. Investopedia / Sabrina Karl Before the run-up, the average had held below $3 for three months—the first sustained stretch in the $2 range since 2021. Read the full article here. -Sabrina Karl Hiring Fell to Lockdown Levels Ahead of Iran War March 31, 2026 01:10 PM EDT Getting a job in February was just as hard as it was in April 2020, when COVID-19 closures were in full swing. The hiring rate—that is, the number of hires as a percentage of total employment—fell to 3.1% in February from 3.4% in January, the Bureau of Labor Statistics said Tuesday. That tied with the previous low in April 2020 and was only lower in 2010, when the economy was pulling out of the Great Recession. There were 6.9 million job openings in February, down from an upwardly revised 7.2 million in January. That figure matched forecasters' expectations in a survey by Dow Jones Newswires and The Wall Street Journal. The number of layoffs remained at 1.7 million, close to historic lows, reinforcing the idea of a low-hiring, low-firing job market. A 'now hiring' sign at the Mega JobNewsUSA South Florida Job Fair held in the Amerant Bank Arena on April 30 in Sunrise, Florida. Joe Raedle / Getty Images The report added detail to data the bureau released earlier, which showed the economy lost 92,000 jobs and the unemployment rate increased to 4.4% in February. Both were signs of a job market slowdown underway on the eve of the Iran war. Read the full article here. -Diccon Hyatt This Nvidia Partner's Stock Is Soaring on a New Deal With the AI Chip Leader and $2 Billion Investment March 31, 2026 12:59 PM EDT A new deal with Nvidia is sending shares of Marvell Technology soaring Tuesday. Shares of Marvell (MRVL) were up over 11% in recent trading after the company announced a $2 billion investment from Nvidia (NVDA) and expanded partnership bringing more of Marvell's semiconductors and networking products into its infrastructure. Nvidia shares climbed about 3%. Nvidia said that the partnership will offer "customers building on NVIDIA architectures greater choice and flexibility in developing next-generation infrastructure" with the addition of custom Marvell products. Nvidia's agreement with Marvell marks the latest in a series of deals this year. Bloomberg / Getty Images Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang told CNBC in a televised interview Tuesday that the move is expected to help grow the total addressable market for both companies, and that Nvidia wants to have a stake in that expanded opportunity for Marvell. Read the full story here. -Aaron McDade Apellis Pharmaceuticals Stock More Than Doubles After Firm Agrees to Be Acquired by Biogen March 31, 2026 12:42 PM EDT Biogen (BIIB) said its deal to buy Apellis Pharmaceuticals (APLS) is expected to be increasingly accretive to adjusted earnings per share beginning in 2027. Apellis shares are seeing benefits immediately. Apellis stock more than doubled Tuesday after the Waltham, Mass.-based firm agreed to be acquired by Biogen for $41 per share in cash, or about $5.6 billion. Its shareholders will also receive a nontransferable contingent value right (CVR) for each Apellis share held, "entitling the holder to receive two payments of $2 per share each, contingent on certain annual global net sales thresholds being met for SYFOVRE," its age-related macular degeneration treatment. Apellis shares, which closed yesterday at $17.09, skyrocketed 135% to more than $40 in recent trading. They now are up 60% in 2026. Biogen said the "financially attractive transaction (is) expected to be increasingly accretive to non-GAAP diluted earnings per share (EPS) starting in 2027 and expected to meaningfully increase Biogen’s non-GAAP EPS compounded annual growth rate (CAGR) through the end of the decade." The deal is expected to close in the second quarter this year, Biogen said. It added the transaction would bring into its fold commercial products that produced $689 million in revenue in 2025, and "are expected to grow at a rate in the mid-to-high teens at least through 2028." Shares of Cambridge, Mass.-based Biogen fell 4.5% and now are up just 2% this year. TradingView The Stock Market Is Having Its Worst Quarter in Years—And Some 'Pretty Rough' Days. Can It Turn Around? March 31, 2026 11:40 AM EDT It’s been one year since “Liberation Day” rewrote the Wall Street playbook. Investors are being put to a different test in 2026. The S&P 500 is down more than 7% since the start of the year, putting the benchmark index on track to post its worst quarter since 2022, with the losses coming entirely after the U.S. and Israel launched strikes on Iran in late February. The ensuing conflict has disrupted oil production, processing, and shipping across the Middle East, causing oil prices to skyrocket. Economists and investors fear higher energy costs will fuel inflation, which was creeping higher before the war began, and weigh on an already wobbly labor market. The S&P 500 has declined more than 7% in Q1, making it the worst quarter for stocks since 2022. Michael Nagle / Bloomberg via Getty Images Around this time last year, the stock market had a meltdown when President Donald Trump revealed his sweeping “Liberation Day” tariffs. After a week of panic, Trump backtracked and the notion of the “TACO trade”—short for “Trump Always Chickens Out,” suggesting that he will adapt policy to market pressure—was born. Investors still talk about the possibility of TACO on the menu, but the dramatic and decisive market movements seen a year ago seem to have been replaced by a grind. “Unfortunately, it doesn't look like the tariff trade is going to be exactly proxied in 2026,” said Gina Martin Adams, chief market strategist at HB Wealth, in an interview with Investopedia. Read the full article here. -Colin Laidley Unilever and McCormick Reach Deal Creating a $65 Billion Food Giant—Here's What Investors Need to Know March 31, 2026 11:18 AM EDT The grocery aisle is getting a new spice, soup, and sauce conglomerate. Hellmann's mayonnaise and Knorr's soup owner Unilever (UL) said Tuesday it's agreed to a deal combining its food brands with McCormick (MKC), known for its spices and condiments like French's mustard and Cholula hot sauce. McCormick said in a press release that it would pay Unilever $15.7 billion in cash and about $29.1 billion in stock of the newly combined company. McCormick and Unilever shares have both fallen in recent weeks amid uncertainty about the terms of the deal as reports of talks emerged. Justin Sullivan / Getty Images Unilever is set to own 9.9% of the company, with Unilever shareholders and McCormick owning 55.1% and 35%, respectively. McCormick said the deal values its business at $21 billion and Unilever's food division at $44.8 billion, valuing the combined entity just above $65 billion. McCormick will retain its name and New York Stock Exchange listing, with executives from both companies set to lead the C-suite and board. Read the full article here. -Aaron McDade Netflix Aims to Expand NFL Slate, Report Says March 31, 2026 11:05 AM EDT Netflix (NFLX) is looking to double the size of its NFL offerings to four games, according to a report from The Wall Street Journal. The streaming giant is in the final year of a three-year agreement to broadcast two games on Christmas, and is reportedly interested in adding two others, potentially an international game during the opening week of the regular season, and another that the NFL has considered adding on the day before Thanksgiving. Other streaming partners including Alphabet's (GOOGL) YouTube and Amazon (AMZN) are also exploring the idea of adding more games to their agreements, the Journal reported. Fans look on in front of a Netflix sign before the NFL game between the Washington Commanders and the Dallas Cowboys at Northwest Stadium on Dec. 25, 2025 in Landover, Md. Scott Taetsch / Getty Images Streaming companies have increasingly turned to live sports in recent years as a new area of content that could draw in new subscribers because of their consistent live viewership numbers. Netflix shares were up about 1.5% in recent trading. -Aaron McDade Prices of Eggs and Meat Are Now Almost as Important as Housing Costs in Decisions on Where to Move March 31, 2026 10:46 AM EDT When people consider finding a new area to move to, rent and mortgage costs are usually the first considerations. But the prices of eggs and meat are almost as important in that decision, according to a new survey showing that persistent inflation is now affecting where people choose to live. Of the 1,248 adults surveyed by Apartments.com recently, 56% said they would consider the daily cost of living, including groceries, dining out and household items, when determining where to live. That isn't far below the 64% that cited housing costs as a factor. Both ranked ahead of utility costs, proximity to services, transportation, and job opportunities. Rising costs for groceries can shape where people choose to live because they directly affect how far a paycheck stretches. Photo by Justin Sullivan / Getty Images “The high percentage of people considering everyday household goods in their move shows how important those expenses are today,” the report said. “Groceries keep getting more expensive, and it's making a big difference in whether people can live comfortably in a city.” The February Consumer Price Index put "food-at-home" inflation at 2.4%—on par with the overall rate. But consumers have faced sharply higher prices on specific items for years. Egg prices, which surged during the 2024 campaign, and more recently meat costs, have rattled shoppers. Read the full article here. -Terry Lane Constellation Energy Shares Sink on Soft Profit Outlook March 31, 2026 09:56 AM EDT Constellation Energy's 2026 business and earnings outlook was a dud for investors. Shares of Constellation Energy (CEG) sank 6% to lead early Nasdaq decliners Tuesday after the Baltimore-based firm issued full-year profit guidance below analysts' expectations. Constellation Energy sees 2026 adjusted operating earnings per share between $11 and $12. The midpoint was well below the $11.97 consensus estimate of analysts surveyed by Visible Alpha. In addition, CEO Joe Dominguez said on the conference call that although he had previously indicated that the company "expected to be done with an important transaction by this call ... we're not ready to announce anything today," according to a transcript provided by AlphaSense, adding that "there is clearly more scrutiny on data center development and so we think it's really important that data center announcements occur when all stakeholders ... are present and prepared to discuss the elements of these important transactions." Constellation Energy shares are down roughly 20% year-to-date. TradingView One Month Into the Iran War, Here Are All the Ways It's Costing Americans March 31, 2026 08:55 AM EDT A month ago, analysts could only project what the Iran war might cost the average American. Now the wide-ranging toll is showing up in everyday budgets and weighing heavily on consumer sentiment. "Americans are often thinking about [the war's costs] in terms of the price of gas," said Layna Mosley, who directs the Sovereign Finance Lab at Princeton University. "But the costs are a lot broader than that." Gas prices are the most visible cost to most Americans, but the price they'll pay for the conflict touches on far more. M. Scott Brauer / Bloomberg / Getty Images The Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development last week revised its U.S. inflation forecast up 1.2 percentage points, setting the 2026 outlook at 4.2%, more than double the Federal Reserve's 2.0% target, as soaring oil prices work their way through the economy. Read the full article here. -Peter Gratton Long Lines at Airports Send Demand for Clear's App—and Stock—Soaring March 31, 2026 08:29 AM EDT Long security lines at the airport have powered a stock-market winner you might not have heard of. Analysts at JP Morgan in a recent note said that while Transportation Security Administration workers' callout rates have started to improve since President Donald Trump signed an executive order to pay TSA agents, they remain elevated. That could keep demand for Clear running high, the analysts said, though downloads of the app have likely peaked. Travelers wait in the Clear security line at Atlanta Hartsfield-Jackson International Airport. Megan Varner / Getty Images As frustrated travelers have contended with longer-than-usual wait times—and Americans have been assaulted by horror stories about the lines in the news and on social media—amid a partial government shutdown, Clear Secure (YOU), which operates the Clear screening system, has been a steady gainer. The stock, up more than 3% on Monday, is up about 40% this year, with most of that coming after the shutdown began in mid-February. Read the full article here. -Kara Greenberg Centessa Pharmaceuticals Stock Skyrockets as Eli Lilly Buys Firm for at Least $6.3B March 31, 2026 08:21 AM EDT Eli Lilly wanted to expand its "capabilities into sleep medicine." Centessa Pharmaceuticals shareholders are reaping the benefits before the bell. U.S.-listed shares of Centessa Pharmaceuticals (CNTA) are skyrocketing nearly 50% in premarket trading Tuesday after the London-based firm and Eli Lilly (LLY) announced the Indianapolis-based drug giant would acquire the clinical-stage company for an initial $6.3 billion in cash. Per the terms of the deal, which is expected to close in the third quarter, Lilly will pay $38 in cash per share plus one non-transferrable contingent value right (CVR) worth up to $9 per share if three milestones are achieved. In total, the deal could be worth $7.8 billion. Lilly, the maker of blockbuster weight-loss drugs Mounjaro and Zepbound, said the acquisition expands its "neuroscience portfolio and capabilities into sleep medicine." Centessa is developing "orexin receptor 2 (OX2R) agonists designed to address the neurobiological system critical to the sleep-wake cycle to treat excessive daytime sleepiness and disorders of impaired wakefulness," the companies said. Lilly shares, which entered the day down about 18% this year, rose 1% before the bell. Eli Lilly agreed to acquire Centessa Pharmaceuticals before the bell Tuesday. Nikos Pekiaridis / NurPhoto via Getty Images Switching Jobs Doesn't Get the Pay Raise It Once Did March 31, 2026 07:44 AM EDT Not too long ago, workers had a clear path to earn more pay: find a better job. But with the job market now showing signs of slowing, there are now fewer opportunities for workers to improve their pay by switching jobs, new research shows. New studies showed that job switchers aren't getting the same kind of pay raises they saw a few years ago. Joe Raedle / Getty Images In January, people who switched jobs received a 4% pay increase, well below the recent peak of around 14% in 2022 and less than half the pre-pandemic 2019 average, according to Bank of America research. And a separate National Bureau of Economic Research (NBER) report found that workers today were half as likely to receive a better-paying outside job offer as they were in the 1980s. Read the full article here. -Terry Lane Bill Ackman Called U.S. Stocks 'Extremely Cheap.' Markets Wavered. What's Next for Investors? March 31, 2026 07:28 AM EDT Advance or retreat? That's the question on investors' minds as the war in Iran enters its fifth week. The Dow Jones Industrial Average, S&P 500 and the Nasdaq rose immediately following President Donald Trump's most recent warning to Iran, but those gains quickly evaporated. "Great progress has been made," Trump said in a Monday morning social media post, saying that "if for any reason a deal is not shortly reached" the U.S. would ramp up attacks on Iran's energy complex. All three major indexes slipped into the red by the afternoon, though, the Dow managed to eke out a slight rise by the close. Stocks finished mostly lower on Monday, though the Dow managed slim gains. Michael Nagle / Bloomberg via Getty Images Nobody knows exactly when, or how, the conflict in Iran will end. But a number of market watchers insist that the pressure it's put on markets has U.S. stocks looking cheap—even as some investors have shown a newfound caution about buying the dip. Read the full article here. -Crystal Kim Stock Futures Rise as Indexes Set to End Worst Quarter Since 2022 March 31, 2026 06:59 AM EDT Futures contracts connected to the Dow Jones Industrial Average were 0.6% higher. TradingView S&P 500 futures also pointed up 0.6%. TradingView Nasdaq 100 futures rose 0.5%.
